# Copilot instructions — nccs-data-core

This repo is the core 990 producer for the NCCS data system. It
processes IRS Statistics of Income (SOI) extracts and the legacy
pre-2012 BMF archive into three contracted parquet/CSV surfaces
that downstream consumers (the `nccsdata` R package, the
dataexplorer API, the sector-in-brief dashboard, research
notebooks) read directly. Changes here ripple outward through
documented contracts.

## Always-on context

When reviewing a PR or answering a question about this repo, first
read the relevant contracts in the sibling `nccs-contracts` repo:

- `nccs-contracts/ARCHITECTURE.md` — the system overview (one page,
  worth re-reading per session).
- `nccs-contracts/CONTRIBUTING.md` — the plan/execute/reconcile
  loop and the tactical-vs-new-ADR-vs-supersede heuristic.
- `nccs-contracts/contracts/core-*.yml` — the three contracts this
  repo produces.
- `nccs-contracts/decisions/` — ADRs that bind producer behavior;
  the ones most relevant to this repo are listed below.

The contracts files are authoritative for what gets published. If a
PR changes producer behavior in a way the contract doesn't reflect,
either the PR description must update the contract YAML (in a
companion PR to `nccs-contracts`) or the change is out of bounds.

## Contracts this repo produces

| Contract | Output path | Producer entrypoint |
|---|---|---|
| `core-990` | `s3://nccsdata/processed/core/{tax_year}/{form}/...` | `R/run_pipeline.R` → `R/08_upload.R` `run_upload()` |
| `core-legacy` | `s3://nccsdata/processed_legacy/core/{tax_year}/{form}/...` | `R/run_legacy_pipeline.R` → `R/08_upload.R` `run_upload_legacy()` |
| `core-panel` | `s3://nccsdata/processed_merged/core/{tax_year}/{form}/...` | `R/run_build_panel.R` → `R/08_upload.R` `run_upload_merged()` |

`core-panel` is a *within-core* form-type union (990 + 990-EZ
unioned into `990combined`; 990-PF as a sibling), not a
cross-dataset BMF×core×efile merge. The cross-dataset merge has
been dropped — see ADR 0016. If a PR talks about "the merged
artifact," confirm whether they mean within-core (this repo's
`core-panel`) or the abandoned cross-dataset one.

## Retired contract

`contracts/core-harmonized.yml` was retired 2026-05-21 per ADR
0015. The harmonize stage (`R/03_harmonize.R` writing to
`s3://nccsdata/intermediate/core/harmonized/`) is an internal
build artifact used for debugging and rehydration; it is NOT a
consumer-facing contract surface. Any PR that adds a new consumer
of `intermediate/core/harmonized/` should be flagged — that path
has no contract and the data flows through `promote_harmonized_to_processed`
to the contracted surfaces.

## What to flag in PR reviews

Path-filtered to keep Opus cost bounded. The agent should review
PRs that touch contract-sensitive files:

- `R/08_upload.R` — the orchestrator. All three contracted
  surfaces are written by this file's three `run_upload*` entry
  points. Changes here directly affect S3 layout.
- `R/run_pipeline.R`, `R/run_legacy_pipeline.R`,
  `R/run_build_panel.R` — top-level invocations.
- `R/03_harmonize.R`, `R/03_legacy_harmonize.R` — schema-shaping
  stage. Column changes here propagate downstream.
- `R/04_derive_combined.R`, `R/04_legacy_merge.R` — produces the
  `990combined` files (the 990 + 990-EZ union) that `core-panel`
  publishes.
- `R/transforms/` — per-column transforms; behavior changes ripple
  to schema.
- `R/06_dictionary.R` — produces the per-partition dictionary CSV
  that the contract YAMLs name as `schema.source`. Changes here
  affect what drift detection sees as the schema.
- `R/09_parquet.R` — parquet copies of the CSV tiers. Not yet
  contract-canonical (CSV is); flag any PR that promotes parquet
  to canonical or changes the dual-publish pattern.
- `R/config.R` — `S3` block; PATHS block. Any path change is a
  contract change.
- `R/aws_s3_sync.R` — the upload helper. Behavior changes here
  affect every contracted output.

Skip review on: tests for pure transforms, the `quality/` reports
themselves, `docs/quality-reports/`, lockfiles, `man/`
autogenerated, IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, TODO.md.

When reviewing a flagged PR, check:

1. **Does the change alter what gets written to S3?** Path,
   filename, schema, compression, file count per partition.
   If yes, the matching `nccs-contracts/contracts/core-*.yml`
   must be updated in a companion PR. Flag if not.
2. **Schema changes.** A new column, a type change, or a renamed
   column ripples to `sector-in-brief-data` (the heaviest external
   consumer) and to the dataexplorer API. The contract YAML's
   `schema.source` points at the per-partition dictionary; that
   should reflect the change.
3. **Manifest emission.** Per ADR 0014, all producers should emit
   a `_manifest.json` with the standard fields. None of this
   repo's three contracts currently emit one — they write quality
   reports (`bmf_master_quality_report.json`-style) which carry
   row counts but no sha256 sums or input ETags. If a PR touches
   `R/08_upload.R` *without* adding manifest support, flag as a
   missed opportunity (not blocking).
4. **Vintage subdirectories.** Per ADR 0013, the three core
   contracts should migrate to `{key_prefix}/v{YYYY.MM}/` with a
   `latest/` mirror. Currently overwriting in place. Same flagging
   principle as manifests.
5. **Within-core vs. cross-dataset confusion.** Per ADR 0016,
   there is no canonical cross-dataset merge and there will not
   be a `nccs-data-merged` repo. If a PR description references
   "the merged producer" or proposes joining BMF data into a core
   output, flag for ADR coordination — the canonical-merge
   ambition is dropped; joins happen consumer-side.
6. **`intermediate/core/harmonized/` consumers.** No external
   consumer should read this path; it has no contract. Flag any
   PR that exposes it to downstream readers or promotes it to a
   non-internal surface.

## Reference ADRs

- [0001 — S3 as contract surface](https://github.com/UrbanInstitute/nccs-contracts/blob/main/decisions/0001-s3-as-contract-surface.md)
- [0003 — Retire Athena for DuckDB](https://github.com/UrbanInstitute/nccs-contracts/blob/main/decisions/0003-retire-athena-for-duckdb.md)
- [0004 — Cadence-aware drift detection](https://github.com/UrbanInstitute/nccs-contracts/blob/main/decisions/0004-cadence-aware-drift-detection.md)
- [0013 — Versioned producer outputs](https://github.com/UrbanInstitute/nccs-contracts/blob/main/decisions/0013-versioned-producer-outputs.md)
- [0014 — Standardize manifest shape](https://github.com/UrbanInstitute/nccs-contracts/blob/main/decisions/0014-standardize-manifest-shape.md)
- [0015 — Core contract surface restructure](https://github.com/UrbanInstitute/nccs-contracts/blob/main/decisions/0015-core-contract-surface-restructure.md)
- [0016 — No canonical cross-dataset merge](https://github.com/UrbanInstitute/nccs-contracts/blob/main/decisions/0016-no-canonical-cross-dataset-merge.md)

ADRs reference each other with `[[adr-slug]]` links inside the
`nccs-contracts` repo; resolve those by reading
`nccs-contracts/decisions/{slug}.md`.

## Reference implementation (sibling repo)

`nccs-data-bmf/R/publish_lookups.R` is the cross-repo reference
for both ADR 0013 (vintage subdirs + `latest/` mirror) and ADR
0014 (manifest emission with sha256-keyed idempotent uploads).
When migrating this repo's `R/08_upload.R` `run_upload*` paths
to the standardized shape, copy from there.

## Style and review tone

- Reviews should focus on contract impact, not personal style.
- When pointing at a contract, link the file at its current path
  in `nccs-contracts` so the author can verify.
- If a PR is a behavior change *and* should have a companion
  contract update *and* should have an ADR, say so plainly — but
  one comment, not three.
- If a PR is internal cleanup with no S3-visible effect, default
  to approving with no comment.
